definition_in_PRW.meaning: net signed flux of information quanta

transport_equation.meaning: J is driven by information density gradient (restoring force) and relaxes with timescale tau. Analogous to Maxwell's H-field equation.

continuity_equation.meaning: J is the current associated with the conserved charge Q = integral s dV
continuity_equation.constraint_on_J: J is the Noether current of the conservation law dQ/dt = 0. This is the strongest structural constraint: J is uniquely defined as the flux vector such that the above holds. In particular, J is NOT defined up to an additive solenoidal field once the continuity equation is taken as primary.

interaction_hamiltonian.constraint: J(x_q, t) must be a real scalar (not a vector) at the qubit location, OR a specific scalar contraction of a vector field with a fixed direction. sigma_z is Hermitian and diagonal. H_int must be Hermitian. Therefore J(x_q, t) must be a real-valued scalar observable.

spectral_density.constraint: The power spectral density of J must be Lorentzian with cutoff 1/tau. Any physical identification of J must reproduce this Lorentzian PSD in the long-wavelength, low-frequency limit.

symmetry_constraints.time_reversal: Under t -> -t: s(x,t) -> s(x,-t) (even), J(x,t) -> -J(x,-t) (odd). This is the standard T-symmetry of a conserved current. Source: continuity equation + PRW balance equations.
symmetry_constraints.spatial_rotation_2D: In 2D (chip plane), J is a 2-component vector: J = (J_x, J_y). Under rotation by angle phi: J_i -> R_ij J_j. H_int = g J * sigma_z requires a scalar from J. Natural choice: J * n_hat (projection onto a fixed direction) or |J| (magnitude, but this breaks linearity in J).
symmetry_constraints.derived_or_assumed: DERIVED from PRW structure + standard current algebra

summary_forced_properties: J is the Noether current of Q = integral s dV (uniquely forced by continuity)
J has units [charge / area / time] = [info / (m^2 s)] in 3D
J is a vector field (3-component in 3D, 2-component in 2D chip plane)
J is odd under time reversal
J is even under spatial parity if s is even (standard current behavior)
The PSD of J at the qubit location must be Lorentzian with scale tau
J(x_q, t) in H_int must enter as a scalar — a projection is needed in >1D
what_is_NOT_forced: The physical medium whose fluctuations produce J
The projection direction n_hat for J * n_hat
The conversion factor between [info] and physical units (J, m, s)

CCA_Ax1_objects.content: Finite set of objects O with composition M
CCA_Ax1_objects.provides_for_J: NO — no metric, no spatial content, no units

CCA_Ax2_causal_order.provides_for_J: PARTIAL — causal order implies a notion of information flow: if event A <= B (A causally precedes B), information can propagate from A to B. This is an arrow. It is not yet a current density, but it is the categorical precursor to one.

CCA_Ax3_time_reversal.content: Involution dagger: M -> M reversing causal order
CCA_Ax3_time_reversal.provides_for_J: PARTIAL — time reversal implies J is odd: J† = -J. This is consistent with the forced property above. The CCA dagger gives J its T-parity without additional assumption.

CCA_Ax4_probability.provides_for_J: PARTIAL — epsilon assigns a probability weight to each morphism. The 'information current' J can be interpreted as the net probability flux across a surface: J(surface) = epsilon(forward morphisms crossing surface) - epsilon(backward morphisms crossing surface). This is a CANDIDATE DEFINITION derivable from CCA.

CCA_Ax5_composition.provides_for_J: PARTIAL — composition tells us how information flows compose. This is needed to extend the local current definition to a field.

candidate_CCA_definition.candidate_definition: J_CCA(Sigma, t) = d/dt [epsilon(morphisms crossing Sigma in + direction) - epsilon(morphisms crossing Sigma in - direction)]
candidate_CCA_definition.physical_interpretation: J_CCA is the net rate of information (probability weight) crossing a spatial surface Sigma per unit area per unit time. This is dimensionally [info / (m^2 s)] in the continuum limit. It is the probability current of the CCA, defined without reference to any physical medium.
candidate_CCA_definition.is_this_derived_from_CCA: PARTIALLY DERIVED: the definition uses Ax2 (causal order to define 'crossing'), Ax3 (dagger to define direction), and Ax4 (epsilon to define the weight). It requires the additional step of taking a continuum limit over the CCA objects — which requires a metric or embedding space that is NOT in Ax1–Ax5.
candidate_CCA_definition.missing_step: The CCA has no spatial metric. Objects in O are abstract; they have no positions. To define J as a spatial density, we need to embed O into a metric space (R^3 or R^2). This embedding is NOT derived from Ax1–Ax5 — it is an additional structural assumption. Without the embedding, J_CCA is defined per surface but not as a local field J(x, t).

minimum_additional_assumptions.name: Spatial embedding
minimum_additional_assumptions.statement: The CCA objects have positions in R^d (d = 2 or 3).
minimum_additional_assumptions.justification: The theory postulates a substrate 'occupying' physical space (CURRENT_C2_ONTOLOGY_MAP Layer 0: '2D chip plane' — classified as D=interpretation). Making this precise requires a map from CCA objects to spatial positions.

minimum_additional_assumptions.name: Continuum limit
minimum_additional_assumptions.statement: The density of CCA objects per unit volume goes to infinity with a fixed object-spacing a → 0.
minimum_additional_assumptions.justification: Required to turn J_CCA (per surface) into J(x,t) (local field).

D1_PRW_current.name: D1_PRW_probability_current
D1_PRW_current.in_words: J_C2 is the net signed flux density of information quanta: the excess of right-movers over left-movers times the walker speed.
D1_PRW_current.source: CURRENT_C2_ONTOLOGY_MAP Layer 0 — this is the existing definition

transformation_properties.spatial_rotation: In 1D: J is a signed scalar. In 3D: J is a vector (J_i = v * (n+_i - n-_i) if n± are direction-resolved). BUT: the 3D PRW is not yet defined (open problem). In 2D chip plane: J = (J_x, J_y).

coupling_to_qubit.scalar_in_H_int: H_int = g J * sigma_z requires J to be a scalar. In 1D: J is already a scalar. In 2D/3D: must project onto a direction: B = n_hat · J(x_q, t). The projection direction n_hat is NOT specified by D1.

coupling_constant_g.derivation: NOT derivable from D1 — remains free

lorentzian_PSD.S0: g^2 * <|J|^2>_0 / (unit area)^2 — depends on g and background density

what_is_missing: 3D generalization of n+, n- (directional resolution in 3D not defined)
Physical identification of information quanta with any material excitation
Projection direction n_hat for the scalar coupling in H_int
D1_PRW_current.verdict: D1 is the only definition already present in the theory. It is internally consistent in 1D. It is undefined in 3D because the 3D PRW is an open problem. It does not connect J_C2 to any physical observable without further assumptions.

D2_CCA_probability_flux.name: D2_CCA_probability_flux
D2_CCA_probability_flux.definition: For a CCA with objects at positions {x_i} ⊂ R^3 with spacing a, and morphisms m: x_i → x_j with weight epsilon(m), define: J_alpha(x, t) = (1/a^3) * sum_{|x_i - x| < a/2} sum_{j: x_j - x_i = a e_alpha} [epsilon(m_{ij})(t) - epsilon(m_{ji})(t)] * v_CCA where e_alpha is the unit vector in direction alpha, v_CCA = a / dt is the CCA morphism speed (lattice constant over time step).
D2_CCA_probability_flux.in_words: J_C2 is the net rate of probability weight flowing in direction alpha through a lattice face, per unit area. It is the discrete probability current of the CCA on its spatial lattice.
D2_CCA_probability_flux.derivation_status: PARTIALLY DERIVED from CCA (Ax2 causal order + Ax4 probability weights) given spatial embedding assumption. NOT derivable from Ax1-Ax5 alone (requires embedding).

units.conversion_factor: Need: [info] = kappa_info * [probability]. kappa_info has units [info] and is a new free parameter unless 'info' is identified with Shannon entropy (dimensionless by convention) or with a physical entropy in [J/K].

information_unit_issue.problem: 'Information' in [info] is the same as 'nat' (natural unit of information). In the C2 theory, s has units [info/m^3]. If [info] = [nat] = dimensionless, then [s] = [1/m^3] (number density), [J] = [1/(m^2 s)] (number flux). This is CONSISTENT with a particle number density: s = number density of information quanta, J = flux of information quanta. Under this identification: [J] = [1/(m^2 s)] = [m^-2 s^-1]. The coupling [g] = [J m^2 s] = [energy] if [info] is dimensionless. g is then an energy — the energy per information quantum.
information_unit_issue.consequence_for_D2: With [info] = dimensionless: J_alpha = number flux of CCA morphisms. kappa_info = 1 (not a new parameter). v_CCA = a/dt = lattice speed. This IDENTIFIES v_CCA with the PRW speed v = c. So c = a/dt = lattice spacing / time step. c is the CCA lattice speed.
information_unit_issue.this_is_new: This identification is not explicitly in any existing C2 document. It arises from following the dimensional analysis to its conclusion.

coupling_to_qubit.natural_scalar: H_int = g J_alpha(x_q, t) sigma_z for a chosen direction alpha. The direction alpha is the direction of the dominant CCA morphism flux at the qubit location — which is determined by the local causal structure (causal order Ax2). This is a partial derivation of the projection direction: alpha = direction of maximal probability flux, determined by the CCA background state.
coupling_to_qubit.g_from_D2: g has units [J] (energy) under the [info]=dimensionless convention. It is the energy transferred per information quantum crossing the qubit. In quantum mechanics, the energy scale is set by the qubit splitting hbar*omega_q. Candidate: g ~ hbar * omega_q * (qubit volume)^{1/3} * (something). This is not yet a derivation — but the dimensional analysis constrains g to be an energy times a length^0 or times a volume. Further: g must be small for the Born approximation to hold: g^2 S0 tau / hbar^2 << hbar omega_q. This is a consistency constraint, not a derivation.

D2_CCA_probability_flux.verdict: D2 is partially derivable from CCA given a spatial embedding. It identifies c with the CCA lattice speed a/dt. It gives a partial derivation of the projection direction. g remains the energy per information quantum — constrained in units but not in value. The spatial embedding is a new assumption.

D3_Helmholtz_ambiguity.name: D3_Helmholtz_ambiguity
D3_Helmholtz_ambiguity.statement: The continuity equation div(J) = -ds/dt determines only the irrotational (longitudinal) part of J via Helmholtz decomposition: J = J_L + J_T where div(J_T) = 0 (transverse/solenoidal part). The continuity equation places NO constraint on J_T.
D3_Helmholtz_ambiguity.consequence: In 3D, J_C2 is underdetermined by the continuity equation alone. The PRW resolves this in 1D (no transverse component exists). In 3D, the PRW must be extended to specify whether J is purely irrotational (gradient of a potential) or has a solenoidal part. The 2D theory assumes J lives in the chip plane, which reduces but does not eliminate this ambiguity.
D3_Helmholtz_ambiguity.physical_relevance: For the qubit coupling: if J_T couples to the qubit, it contributes to dephasing without affecting the continuity equation. The existing theory implicitly assumes J is irrotational (derivable from a potential phi: J = -c^2 tau grad phi for steady state). This is a hidden assumption that should be made explicit.
D3_Helmholtz_ambiguity.verdict: AMBIGUITY — requires additional constraint (irrotational J, or specified J_T)

step3_candidate_definitions.reason_D2_strongest: D2 is the only candidate that connects J_C2 to the CCA axioms in a derivable way (given spatial embedding). It identifies c = a/dt (lattice speed), which is the first non-trivial result: c is the CCA lattice spacing divided by the CCA time step. This is not derivable from Ax1-Ax5 alone but is forced once the spatial embedding is made.

new_assumptions: Spatial embedding of CCA (positions x_i in R^3)
Projection direction alpha = direction of dominant CCA flux

autocorrelation.S0: c^2 * 2 * n0  where n0 = CCA morphism density [m^{-3}]
autocorrelation.tau: 1/(2 lambda) = mean free time between reversals

dephasing_rate.substituting_D2: Gamma_phi = (g^2 / hbar^2) * 2 * (c^2 * 2 n0) * tau = (g^2 / hbar^2) * 4 n0 c^2 tau
dephasing_rate.c_under_D2: c = a / dt  (CCA lattice speed -- determined by CCA geometry)
dephasing_rate.n0_under_D2: n0 = CCA morphism density -- NOT determined by Ax1-Ax5

spatial_correlator.under_D2: xi_c = 2 * (a/dt) * tau. If a and dt are fixed by the CCA geometry, and tau is measured, then xi_c is predicted from the CCA lattice parameters. This would be the first non-free prediction of xi_c. BUT: a/dt = c is still free unless the CCA geometry specifies a and dt.

fixed_by_D2: Functional form of J_C2 (probability flux of CCA morphisms)
Units of J_C2 ([m^{-2} s^{-1}] if info=dimensionless)
Time-reversal and parity properties of J_C2
Lorentzian form of S_JJ(omega) — preserved from PRW
still_free_after_D2: a (CCA lattice spacing) -- not in Ax1-Ax5
dt (CCA time step) -- not in Ax1-Ax5
n0 (CCA morphism density) -- not in Ax1-Ax5
g (coupling energy per quantum) -- constrained in units but not value
Projection direction alpha -- partially constrained by local CCA flux direction
what_D2_fixes_vs_leaves_free.new_constraint_from_D2: c = a/dt is a relationship between three quantities that were previously independent. Once a and dt are fixed by the CCA, c follows. This is a genuine new constraint — but a and dt are still free.

gap_0a_spatial_embedding.what: A map from CCA objects to positions in R^d
gap_0a_spatial_embedding.why_needed: Without positions, J cannot be a spatial field
gap_0a_spatial_embedding.physical_content: The CCA lives in physical space. This requires specifying the dimensionality d and the embedding map. For the chip geometry: d=2, with the qubit in the plane.
gap_0a_spatial_embedding.what_it_gives: J_C2 becomes a field on R^d, not just an abstract flux
gap_0a_spatial_embedding.is_it_reasonable: YES: the theory already assumes a 2D chip plane (CURRENT_C2_ONTOLOGY_MAP Layer 0, classified as D=interpretation). Making it an explicit assumption is just promoting an implicit interpretation to an axiom.

gap_0b_lattice_scale.what: The CCA lattice spacing a (and time step dt = a/c)
gap_0b_lattice_scale.why_needed: Determines c = a/dt and n0 (morphism density ~ 1/a^d)
gap_0b_lattice_scale.physical_content: a is the fundamental length scale of the information substrate. It sets the UV cutoff of the theory. In a discretized CCA: a ~ Planck length (if fundamental), or a ~ qubit spacing (if emergent from chip geometry), or a ~ phonon wavelength at the Debye cutoff (if phononic).
gap_0b_lattice_scale.what_it_gives: Fixes c, n0, xi_c as functions of a and tau

Planck_scale.c_if_dt_is_Planck_time: c = a / t_P = speed of light = 3e8 m/s
Planck_scale.comment: This gives c = speed of light, which contradicts the assumption c ~ v_acoustic ~ 6000 m/s. Not compatible with the existing experimental context.

qubit_spacing.c_if_measured_tau: c = a / dt = a * 2*lambda  ... dt = 1/(2*lambda*c) -- circular
qubit_spacing.comment: c is still not fixed unless dt is independently determined.

decoherence_length.a: xi_c / (2 * c * tau / xi_c)  -- circular without fixing c
decoherence_length.comment: Cannot determine a from decoherence data without knowing c first.

gap_0b_lattice_scale.conclusion: No physically motivated choice of a is available from the existing theory. a is genuinely free.
gap_0b_lattice_scale.classification: NEW FREE PARAMETER (a is not in Ax1-Ax5)

gap_0c_morphism_density.what: n0 = density of active CCA morphisms per unit volume
gap_0c_morphism_density.why_needed: Determines S0 = c^2 * 2 n0 in dephasing formula

gap_0d_coupling_energy.what: g = energy transferred per information quantum to qubit
gap_0d_coupling_energy.dimensional_constraint: g must satisfy: g^2 * S0 * tau / hbar^2 ~ Gamma_phi ~ 1/T2. For T2 ~ 100 microseconds: g^2 * S0 * tau ~ hbar^2 / T2 ~ (1e-34)^2 / 1e-4 ~ 1e-64 J^2. With S0 = c^2 * n0 and tau ~ 1e-6 s: g^2 ~ 1e-64 / (c^2 * n0 * 1e-6). For c ~ 6000 m/s and n0 ~ 1e15 m^{-3}: g ~ 1e-34 J ~ hbar. This is consistent with g ~ hbar, suggesting g is of order the quantum of action times some frequency.
gap_0d_coupling_energy.candidate_expression: g = hbar * omega_0 / c  where omega_0 is a substrate frequency
gap_0d_coupling_energy.classification: CONSTRAINED BY DIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS but not uniquely fixed

genuine_derivation: J_C2 is the CCA probability flux (from Ax2, Ax4, spatial embedding)
J_C2 is odd under T-reversal (from Ax3 = dagger involution)
J_C2 is a vector field in d dimensions (from spatial embedding)
The Lorentzian PSD of J_C2 follows from the PRW structure (existing result)
c = a/dt is forced once a and dt are fixed (new structural result)
still_requires_external_input: Spatial embedding (new axiom promoting existing interpretation)
Coupling energy g (constrained but not fixed)

is_this_progress.reason: Before this derivation: J_C2 had no connection to anything outside the PRW. After D2: J_C2 is the CCA probability flux, derivable given spatial embedding. This gives J_C2 a physical interpretation (causal information flow) and identifies c as the CCA lattice speed. The identification c = a/dt is the first structural constraint on c — it does not fix c's value, but it says what c IS: the speed at which causal information propagates at the lattice scale. This is a genuine, if partial, advance.
is_this_progress.what_is_not_progress: We still have three free parameters (a, n0, g). The experiment cannot be designed until these are constrained. The spatial embedding is a new assumption, not a theorem. D2 does not select a unique speed in 3D — if the CCA has directional structure (anisotropic causal order), different directions can have different lattice spacings and thus different c.
